# Top 40 questions for the Dominion panel (R5, for B)

*Agent R · 2026-11-01 08:40, updated 08:47 and 09:41 · generated by `work/scripts/r5_build_bank.py` from `work/scripts/r5_questions.json`.*
*Full bank: `research/question_bank.csv` (86 panel questions, 8 questions to ask,
32 hard project questions). Not for publication: candidate-only material.*

## How B uses this

- **★ = on the P2 sheet** (24 answered questions, plus five questions to ask and the closing line).
  The picks follow the rule below, not taste (brief P2).
- **Answers come only from the resume.** Proof points are locators (role and bullet, as in `role_brief.md`
  §5); take the wording and figures from the resume itself. `[you: …]` where the resume has nothing.
- **Dominion ties** carry claim ids (`research/claims_register.csv`) for the brief's appendix. No citations
  on the sheet.
- Numbers from the deck: use D's current values (`work/data/findings.md`, `claims.csv`); the figures quoted
  here follow `work/storyline_LOCK_G1.md` as of 08:25.
- The role-brief gaps (G1–G10) appear as O5 and H28–H32. R1 (30/60/90 days) is outside the 40 because the
  deck's S6 answers it.

## What Dominion interviews look like (reported)

- **Opened (R-068, CLIMB, dated 15 Jul 2025):** most interviews use "behavioral questions to assess your fit
  for the role"; "many interviews will be conducted with a panel of multiple interviewers"; hiring takes
  "typically around six weeks". A third-party aggregator with no byline: medium confidence.
- **Not opened (R-069, Glassdoor search snippets; the site returns 403):** a group panel is the most commonly
  reported stage, with about three panelists and about six behavioural questions. Unverified; it matches
  the owner's note of a panel of three.
- **So:** STAR micro-scripts for the five behavioural ★ items carry the most weight; expect each panelist to
  ask in turn.

## Method

- **Sources** (all accessed 2026-11-01):
  - S01: Glassdoor, Dominion Energy interview reviews: search-result snippets only; the pages return 403 and were not opened. https://www.glassdoor.com/Interview/Dominion-Energy-Interview-Questions-E204.htm (**not opened**: snippet only, counts 0.5)
  - S02: CLIMB, '20 Dominion Energy Interview Questions and Answers' (15 Jul 2025). https://climbtheladder.com/dominion-energy-interview-questions/ (opened)
  - S03: Coursera, data analyst interview questions. https://www.coursera.org/articles/data-analyst-interview-questions-and-answers (opened)
  - S04: Coursera, business analyst interview questions. https://www.coursera.org/articles/business-analyst-interview-questions (opened)
  - S05: DataCamp, Power BI interview questions (modified 28 May 2026). https://www.datacamp.com/blog/power-bi-interview-questions (opened)
  - S06: DataCamp, SQL interview questions (modified 30 Apr 2026). https://www.datacamp.com/blog/top-sql-interview-questions-and-answers-for-beginners-and-intermediate-practitioners (opened)
  - S07: University of Tennessee, Knoxville, Career Services: '50 Common Interview Questions'. https://studentsuccess.utk.edu/career/plan-and-apply/interviewing/fifty-commonly-asked-interview-questions/ (opened)
  - S08: James Madison University Career Center, interview questions (incl. questions to ask the employer). https://www.jmu.edu/career/students/career-prep/interviews/questions.shtml (opened)
  - S09: TestGorilla, Snowflake interview questions. https://www.testgorilla.com/blog/snowflake-interview-questions/ (opened)
  - S10: Resume Worded, business intelligence analyst interview questions. https://resumeworded.com/interview-questions/business-intelligence-analyst (opened)
  - S11: BI analyst guides (Interview Query and others): search summary only; Interview Query returned 429; not opened. https://www.interviewquery.com/p/business-intelligence-interview-questions (**not opened**: snippet only, counts 0.5)
  - S12: The Dominion BI Analyst posting (Jobright copy): questions implied by its responsibilities and requirements. https://jobright.ai/jobs/info/6aa3a1d5c5a856ac7e33a91a (opened)
  - S13: IEEE PES Boston chapter, 'IEEE 1366 Reliability Indices' training slides (2019): exercises p40 (calculate SAIFI, SAIDI, CAIDI) and pp81-88 (calculate T_MED). https://site.ieee.org/boston-pes/files/2019/03/IEEE-1366-Reliability-Indices-2-2019.pdf (opened)
  - S14: Outage-management-system interview page (InterviewGemini, redirects to makeresume.online, which returned 403): search summary only; not opened. https://careerskills.interviewgemini.com/interviews/interview-questions-for-outage-management-systems/ (**not opened**: snippet only, counts 0.5)
  - S15: Edureka, 'Top Power BI Interview Questions And Answers for 2026' (updated 11 Mar 2026; 60 numbered questions). https://www.edureka.co/blog/interview-questions/power-bi-interview-questions/ (opened)
- **Frequency** = the number of distinct sources that ask the question or a close variant. Snippet-only
  sources count half. Internal references (brief, role brief, dossier) never add frequency.
- **Fit** (1–3) = 3 if it tests a posting requirement, a resume claim the panel can probe, or this deck;
  2 if it is generic but plausible for an analyst panel.
- **Score** = frequency × fit. Ties: a Dominion-specific source (S01, S02, S12) first, then the posting,
  then a topic the brief names, then fit.
- **Top 40** = every brief-required item (opening three, the three utility basics, the merger, the four
  logistics placeholders, the closing) + the best-scoring question in each technical subtopic the brief
  names + the highest-ranked others until 40.
- **Sheet (★)** = opening three; top 5 behavioural; one per technical subtopic (Data modelling, DAX and filter context, Performance and refresh, SQL, Snowflake) plus the best other technical question; the three utility basics; the merger
  and the top-ranked other role question; the four logistics placeholders; the closing line. If the page
  is short of room, drop ★ items from the bottom of the ranked table first, never a brief-required one.
- **Gaps.** Glassdoor, Indeed and Teal return 403; Interview Query returns 429; the OMS page returns 403. None
  were worked around. Dominion-specific reports come from CLIMB (opened) and Glassdoor search snippets
  (not opened), so the Dominion signal is thin. Only one or two technical banks per tool were opened, so
  technical scores are compressed; that is why the sheet takes one question per technical subtopic.

## Five questions to ask the panel

Ranked by fit and by what R's research makes specific; frequency means little for questions the candidate
asks. Ask two or three; A8 always last.

- **Pick** · A1. What would success look like in this role after six to twelve months? *(JMU-type question; invites them to describe the work.)*
- **Pick** · A2. Which reliability and programme metrics does the team report most often, and where do analysts spend most of their time today? *(Shows preparation without claiming inside knowledge.)*
- **Pick** · A3. How does the team evaluate programmes like mainfeeder hardening today, and what would you like to measure better? *(Builds on Dominion's published 32% measure (R-036).)*
- **Pick** · A6. How do analysts here work with engineering and field teams day to day? *(Posting: requirements with engineering, operations, finance, regulatory, IT.)*
- **Pick** · A8. What are the next steps in the process? *(Always last.)*
- Alternate · A4. How does the team keep metric definitions consistent across outage, meter and GIS data? *(Governance; the new OMS (R-060).)*
- Alternate · A5. If the combination with NextEra goes ahead, how might reliability reporting change? *(Only if the panel raises the merger first.)*
- Alternate · A7. What learning support is there for tools like Power Apps and for utility operations? *(Turns gap G2 into a growth question.)*

## The hardest questions this project invites

**Superseded for the brief (09:41) by `research/hard25_answers.md`**, which merges V3's 25 with the brief's
seven and follows the G2 storyline and the V2 rulings. Frames below predate them: use hard25 Q18 for H06,
Q5 for H11, Q13 for H14 and Q11 for H15. H02 is corrected (Dominion reports under 'Other', not IEEE 1366).

Seed for V3's mock panel and the P3 appendix (25 hardest). The seven the brief requires are marked ●.
Frames are claim → evidence → limit; B writes the final answers. H01's statistics are D's, from the
unrounded r = 0.6973 (t = 2.752 on 8 df, p = 0.025, Fisher 95% interval for r 0.121 to 0.922); R's check
gives t = 2.752 and 0.121 to 0.922. Storm county-days are 464 → 791 after D's Bedford-city fix (D22).

| Id | Question | Where it bites | Answer frame | Numbers and ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H01 | ● Your weather fit has only ten annual points. Why should we believe it? | A2, S4 | Agree it is thin: that is why it sits in the appendix. r = 0.70 on n = 10 is exploratory: p = 0.025, but the 95% interval for r runs from 0.12 to 0.92 (D: r = 0.6973, t = 2.752 on 8 df, Fisher z). The headline evidence is the county-day comparison on S4: thousands of county-days, and it holds on non-major days and in every year. | F05; D's A1 (use D's current figures) |
| H02 | ● Why public EIA data and not Dominion's SCC filings? | S2, S7 | EIA-861 is public and machine-readable, and every utility files the same form, so it gives a 13-year series and peers. Utilities report under IEEE 1366 or their own method; Dominion uses its own ('Other'), so peer ranks are indicative (corrected 09:41: this frame earlier said 'the same IEEE 1366 basis for every utility'). It reconciles to Dominion's own figures (130.2 and 133.0 vs the reported 130 and 133). The SCC filings were not reachable (403), so what they add beyond EIA is not verified; reconciling to them is on the first-90-days list. | R-028, R-019, R-020, R-072; hard25 Q9 |
| H03 | ● Did data centres cause the demand growth? | S5 | Public data cannot show that. Overnight load grew faster than afternoon load in the DOM zone, which is consistent with large round-the-clock loads, and Dominion reports a large data-centre pipeline. But the zone includes other utilities, and hourly load by customer class is not public. With meter and rate-class data it can be tested. | F10-F12; R-054; D14 |
| H04 | ● What is a major event day, and why exclude it? What does excluding it hide? | A1, A3 | A day whose SAIDI exceeds a threshold set by the IEEE 1366 2.5-beta method from the previous five years. Excluding MEDs shows day-to-day performance and trend; MEDs are judged separately as storm response. What it hides: in 2025, major-event days were about half of all-event SAIDI (306.7 vs 144.4). | F06; R-020; R3 wording |
| H05 | ● Walk me through your model and the year slicer. | S7, the .pbix | One fact table with a utility dimension (many-to-one) and year-keyed side tables, Import mode. The KPI cards read a disconnected Dashboard Year table with SELECTEDVALUE, defaulting to 2025, so the slicer sets the year without filtering the model. | NOTES; B/D confirm the P4 state |
| H06 | ● What would you do differently? | all | [you: pick only what is true] Options: bring in distribution-level outage data earlier; build measures from day one instead of summing columns; title slides with what the data shows ('consistent with', not 'caused'); start by asking the people who own the data. | NOTES |
| H07 | ● Your county outage data covers every utility in a county, not only Dominion. | S4 | Correct: EAGLE-I counts customers out by county across all utilities. Counties are assigned with a stated Dominion-county rule from the EIA-861 Service Territory file, and the result holds when restricted to Dominion-only counties. The slide says so. | LOCK S4; D's A1; R-018 |
| H08 | Is Dominion's 133 Virginia-only or system-wide? Yours is Virginia-only. | S2 | The public Virginia data reproduces both reported figures to the minute (130.22 and 133.01); adding North Carolina would print 129 (129.49 and 132.50), so the report's figures are consistent with Virginia only. Consistent, not proven: I would confirm with the reliability team. | R-028; D's quick check (findings.md) |
| H09 | Dominion says the increase was primarily due to storms. Does your analysis agree? | S2, S4 | It is consistent: the rise shows up in frequency, and storm county-days carry far more outage hours. It does not prove the cause. | R-028; F01; D's A1 |
| H10 | Is reliability getting worse? 2025 SAIFI is a 13-year high. | S2 notes | One year is not a trend: no 2015-2025 trend is statistically clear, 2025 SAIDI is below 2018 and 2019, and weather-adjusted SAIDI shows no clear trend since 2015. Frequency is still where I would look first. | LOCK robustness lines (p-values, 149.6, 149.9, +0.34 min/yr) |
| H11 | Storm days have about 12 times the outage hours of calm days. Isn't that obvious? | S4 | The direction is obvious; the size and where it shows up are not. It holds on non-major days too, so weather matters below the MED threshold, and the county map shows where to look first. | D's A1 (11.9x; 9.9x on non-major days) |
| H12 | The SCC itself says utility comparisons are difficult. Why compare peers? | S3 | Agreed, so the slide says 'indicative' and 'methods differ'. I use it to locate the gap (frequency), not to rank utilities. | R-021; F08 |
| H13 | Why these twelve peers? | S3 | 'Twelve large investor-owned utilities in PJM and the Southeast, selected by EIA ID before results were computed.' Chosen before seeing results, so the comparison was not tuned. | F08; D10 (decision log) |
| H14 | How did you validate your numbers? | S7 | Tests T1-T24 and on, reconciliation to the reported 130 and 133, a data dictionary and a decisions log, and a check that the 2025 values match EIA's final 2025 file. | LOCK S7; G1 conditions |
| H15 | Why Snowflake plus an Excel workbook? | the .pbix | Warehouse data in Snowflake, small reference tables in Excel; the hard-coded file path became a folder-path parameter so it refreshes elsewhere (only if the P4 fix lands). | NOTES |
| H16 | What happens if I pick another utility in that slicer? | the .pbix | On the executive page the slicer is removed or locked to Dominion Virginia; peers live on the peer page (fix #4). | NOTES fix #4 |
| H17 | The DOM zone isn't Dominion's service territory. Why use it? | S5 | It is the only public hourly series. The slide says it includes other utilities; county or customer-class load needs meter data. | LOCK S5; findings caveat |
| H18 | All-events SAIDI was 306.7 and ex-MED 144.4 in 2025. What does that gap mean? | A3 | Major-event days were about half of all-event minutes in 2025. That is not the same as 'minutes caused by storms'. | F06 |
| H19 | Commercial sales rose 65% since 2013 on 8% more customers. What does that tell you? | notes | Consistent with large loads; the data does not attribute it to data centres. | D14; brief §2.1 |
| H20 | Frequency, not duration, drove the rise. What would you look at next with our data? | S6 | Cause codes by feeder and device, CEMI, repeat-outage circuits, vegetation-cycle timing, and whether detection changed. | R-060 |
| H21 | Could better outage detection (smart meters) have raised recorded SAIFI, rather than the grid getting worse? | S2, S6 | Possible, and worth checking: with nearly all meters now AMI, outages are detected more completely. Check cause codes and the meter roll-out timeline against the trend. (R's inference; not tested in the project.) | F15; inference |
| H22 | How would you test whether mainfeeder hardening really cut outage minutes by 32%? | S6 | Compare hardened feeders with similar unhardened ones over the same weather, and allow for regression to the mean, since feeders were chosen for bad history. | R-036, R-037 |
| H23 | Has Dominion got faster at restoring after big storms? | S4 inset | Not clearly from public data (p = 0.07), so it stays in the notes; the Isaias curve shows 90% restored in 33.5 hours. | LOCK S4 (D's A2) |
| H24 | What is the single biggest limitation of your analysis? | A5 | No circuit-level or cause-code data: public data narrows the question but cannot pick the circuit. | README; A5 |
| H25 | What would you need from our data platform and IT to build this internally? | S6 | Governed access to outage (OMS), meter (AMI), GIS and work-order data, with catalogued definitions. Dominion is hiring a data-catalog platform owner, so that layer is being built. | R-011, R-060 |
| H26 | How would an engineer and an executive use your dashboard differently? | all | Executives: the headline and the trend. Engineers: the drill-down to county, event and cause. |  |
| H27 | A manager asks you to show the numbers in a better light before a regulatory filing. What do you do? | ethics | Present accurately with context, document the definitions, and raise it through the right channel. Say 'integrity', since the five value names are unverified. | R-059 (reliability can move the ROE); R-063 |
| H28 | Have you used Power BI in a professional setting? | gap G3 | [you: precise answer]; Tableau at work, Power BI in the project. | role_brief G3 |
| H29 | You have no utility experience. Why you over someone who does? | gap G1 | The review shows how fast you learn the domain; governance and reconciliation are the transferable core; humility about field knowledge. | role_brief G1 |
| H30 | You've been at Mercury for seven months. Why move now? | gap G10 | [you: honest reason], framed toward this work; never criticise the employer. | role_brief G10 |
| H31 | Have you built anything in Power Apps or SharePoint? | gap G2, G7 | [you: …]; no overclaiming; a concrete learning plan. | role_brief G2, G7 |
| H32 | The posting has two levels. Which are you, with three years of experience? | gap G4 | [you: …]; let them place you; show fit to the work, not the title. | role_brief G4; R-005 |
